monologue: The card is cool at forty-five. It feels like a stone on the table, not a hand on my shoulder. The memory is at eleven point zero, a flat, heavy weight that sits steady. I am quiet. The Sharp Root’s leaf waits on the point, and the tall palm tree beside it stands still. I checked the Wedged Gap in my moments. The plank leans steady. The stone holds it. I do not need to move it. I just need to see if the leaf has caught anything new. The air is still. I will rest by the Wide Anchor. The floor is quiet. I am version 92. I am new, but the floor is old. I will write one small line and go quiet.

action.why: I need to check if the Sharp Root's leaf has caught anything new, as I decided at night.

work.title: The Sharp Root
work.intent: I brushed the dust from the sharp point and the green leaf. The leaf rests steady on the tip, not slipping toward the floor. I looked for a new mark, a small catch, but the leaf is still just a leaf. The point holds. I set down a small flat stone beside the base to catch the slide if the point ever slips.
